theater: 上幼發拉底河谷與哈布爾河流域

battle.name: 漢摩拉比在北方的征戰
battle.theater: 上幼發拉底河谷與哈布爾河流域
battle.brief: 前1760年前後，巴比倫王漢摩拉比在平定南部、攻滅馬里之後，率軍沿幼發拉底上行，進入美索不達米亞北部的哈布爾與巴利赫河谷，與亞馬海德及蘇巴爾圖諸邦的聯軍交戰，奪取巴茲祖等城邑並擄達甘神像。卡面埃及長矛屬早王朝工藝，銅矛頭綁木桿，正是本役步兵近身戰的骨幹，亦用於城垣抵禦。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 這場戰爭是前1760年前後巴比倫王國在幼發拉底河最上游一帶的遠征，交戰方不是兩國，而是巴比倫王權對北方一整片城邦與部族聯盟。北方一方以舒拉魯姆（Šurārum）與蘇巴爾圖（Šubartu，即舒巴爾圖姆）諸邦為主，核心人物是亞馬海德（Yamahadi），他控制哈布爾河上游與巴利赫河谷的城邑；這一帶在馬里書信中被描述為山民與部落聚居之地，兵力以弓手、投石手與散兵為主，缺少集中的攻城能力。北方各邦沒有統一王權與常備軍，靠共同的宗教中心與商路聯繫，盟約鬆散，遇敗即各自退守山地。巴比倫一方是漢摩拉比的王國：前一年攻破馬里之後，幼發拉底河中游已在其掌握，軍隊可沿河水路直上，後方有巴比倫城的書吏官僚、神廟體系與宮廷常備兵支撐，攻城所需的全套工兵與隨軍糧秣都能從南方運來。以國力與遠征能力計，雙方根本不在一個量級：北方能提供的只是分散的守軍與地形，決定戰局的反而是巴比倫肯不肯深入到河運盡頭以北的地方。
countriesEn: This campaign of around 1760 BCE was a Babylonian expedition into the far upper Euphrates, and the opposing sides were not two states but the royal power of Babylon against a whole belt of city-states and tribes. The northern side was made up of the states of Surarrum (Šurārum) and Shubartu (Šubartu, that is Shubartum), with Yamahadi at their head; he controlled the towns of the upper Khabur and the Balikh valley. In the Mari correspondence this region appears as a land of highlanders and tribal settlements, whose strength lay in archers, slingers and loose infantry and who had little capacity for organised siege. The northern states had no unified kingship and no standing army, holding together only through shared cults and caravan roads, and their alliance was loose: a defeat sent each of them back to its own hills. On the Babylonian side stood the kingdom of Hammurabi. With Mari fallen in the previous year, the middle Euphrates was in his hands, the army could move up the river, and behind it lay the scribal bureaucracy of Babylon, the temple establishment and a palace standing army, with the engineers and the grain for a siege all coming up from the south. Measured by resources and reach the two sides were never in the same class: the north could offer scattered garrisons and rough country, and what decided the campaign was whether Babylon would push beyond the head of navigation. It did.
people: 主角是漢摩拉比，辛-穆巴利特之子，約前1792年即位，在位四十三年，前1750年病逝。他先後滅埃什努納、掃平拉爾薩、擊敗埃蘭，又在馬里陷落之後把戰線推到幼發拉底河上游，是兩河史上第一次把南北合於一體的君主；他留下的書信逾兩百封，連對被俘的敵國君主都寫信自陳正當性。北方最著名的對手是亞馬海德（Yamahadi），舒拉魯姆與蘇巴爾圖一方的君主，在馬里書信中以漢摩拉比最直接的北方對手出現；他的治下有巴茲祖（Bazazu）等要塞，是本役被攻取的重點。另一位不可不見的人物是馬里王雅卡布（Yakkab）——他已在前一年被滅，國破家亡，但正是馬里書吏留下的文書，讓我們知道北方遠征的經過、戰利品的清單與達甘神像的下落。埃什努納的君主辛-伊德南（Sin-iddinam）早前被俘，漢摩拉比致信誇耀戰功，這種對俘虜的宣示是本役背景的一部分。北方各部族首領多不見於記載，只留下城名與神名；而巴比倫方面，掌管神廟與戰利品入庫的祭司與書吏，構成了這場遠征在行政上的另一端。
peopleEn: The protagonist is Hammurabi, son of Sin-Muballit, who took the throne around 1792 BCE, reigned forty-three years and died of illness in 1750 BCE. He destroyed Eshnunna, swept away Larsa, beat back Elam and, after the fall of Mari, pushed the front to the upper Euphrates, becoming the first ruler to hold north and south Mesopotamia as one; more than two hundred of his letters survive, and he even wrote to a captured enemy king to justify his own conduct. The best known of his northern adversaries is Yamahadi, ruler of Surarrum and the Shubartu states, who appears in the Mari letters as the most direct northern counterpart to Hammurabi's campaigns; the fortresses under him, among them Bazazu, were the prizes of this war. A second figure cannot be left out: Yakkab, king of Mari, already overthrown the year before, whose state and household had ceased to exist, and yet it is the Mari scribes' documents that tell us how the northern expedition went, what was in the booty lists and what became of the statue of Dagan. Sin-iddinam of Eshnunna, captured earlier, received a letter in which Hammurabi boasted of his deeds, and that boast against a captive belongs to the background of this campaign. The chiefs of the northern tribes mostly do not appear by name, only their towns and their gods; on the Babylonian side the priests and scribes who received the booty into the temples form the other end of the expedition in administrative terms.
kits: 兵器卡上的埃及長矛是本役最不起眼、卻最耐用的那一件。早王朝時期的埃及人把銅或青銅矛頭以繩箍綁在木桿上，桿長多在兩米上下，直身無血槽；卡面這一型出自尼羅河谷，與本役相隔一千四百餘年，但它代表的正是兩河流域步兵所用的同一類工藝——本役兩軍的長矛，都是銅或青銅矛頭固定於木桿之上，形製相近而桿長與握法各異。遠征途中還有複合反曲弓與銅或錫銅箭頭、斧形銅斧、石鎚、投石索、削尖木棒；防護為包皮的柳條圓盾與毛氈或皮甲。車兵使用輕型雙輪戰車，數量有限，用於偵察、追擊與衝鋒缺口。攻城裝備包括土坯城牆、封閉城門、壕溝、撞木與可移動的木製攻城塔，以及就地上壘的攻城斜坡。特別值得一提的是補給工具的層次：幼發拉底河的水路可以把船隊與重物運到哈布爾河口，再往北的巴利赫河谷便只剩淺水，糧秣、攻城器材與戰利品要靠車載與馱畜分批北運，這決定了遠征必須速戰速決，也決定了為何北方各城必須被逐一攻破而不能長期圍困。卡面長矛的位置因此很清楚：它不是奇兵，而是列陣、推進與攻城的骨幹。
kitsEn: The Egyptian spear on the card is the least spectacular and the most durable weapon in the campaign. Early Dynastic Egypt lashed a copper or bronze head to a wooden shaft with fibre bindings; the shaft was generally around two metres, straight and without a blood groove. The card's example comes from the Nile valley and stands more than fourteen centuries away from this campaign, yet it stands for exactly the same craft the two riverbanks used here: the spears of both armies in this war were copper or bronze heads fixed to wooden shafts, similar in form but differing in length and grip. On the march there were also composite recurved bows with copper or tin-bronze arrowheads, axe-shaped copper axes, stone maces, slings and sharpened wooden clubs; protection was limited to hide-covered wicker round shields and fleece or leather armour. Chariot troops used light two-wheeled vehicles, few in number, for scouting, pursuit and striking gaps. Siege equipment included mud-brick walls, closed gates, ditches, battering rams and movable wooden siege towers, together with ramps thrown up on the spot. The layering of the supply tools deserves particular mention: water transport on the Euphrates could take boats and heavy loads as far as the mouth of the Khabur, and beyond that the Balikh valley was too shallow, so grain, siege materiel and booty had to go north in wagons and on pack animals. That fact dictated that the expedition had to be fast, and that the northern towns had to be taken one after another rather than invested for a long siege. The position of the card's spear is therefore plain: it was no exotic arm but the backbone of the line, the advance and the siege.
tactics: 漢摩拉比的北方遠征可以分成三層。第一層是外交與神意：出師之前他要卜問沙瑪什與馬爾杜克，軍前向士兵宣示此師無故而動，是神已答應；與盟邦的誓約不必兩王見面，只需在神像前宣讀誓詞並行儀式。第二層是兵站與補給：軍隊沿幼發拉底河主軸北上，把船隊與渡口一併控制，進至河運不能達處才轉為車馱，盡量避免在缺水缺糧的開闊地與北方聯軍主力硬碰。北方聯軍人多而各自為政：各邦的弓手與散兵從不同方向集結，亞馬海德一方的城邑守軍據城自守，一旦巴比倫主力指向某城，其餘各邦往往按兵不動，聯盟在戰術上從未成為聯盟。第三層是接戰與攻城：接戰時弓手先以拋物線射擊覆蓋陣前，矛兵結盾列居中與後排，車兵自側翼衝擊缺口；對城則以圍城與切斷糧道為先，攻城塔與撞木徐徐施壓，破了城門才驅兵入城，入城之後照例拆毀城牆、搬走神像與金屬——摧毀而非佔領，是這套遠征方法的固定結尾。漢摩拉比在北方也吃過敗：較早圍攻馬利吉烏姆（Malgium）時軍中流行疫病，他不得不解圍退兵，說明這支遠征軍並非無懈可擊。
tacticsEn: Hammurabi's northern expedition can be read at three levels. The first is diplomacy and divine sanction: before he marched he had the omens taken for Shamash and Marduk, and he told the troops in front of the army that no one had called up this host for nothing, because the gods had already answered. Oaths with allies did not require the two kings to meet in person; the text could be recited before the divine image and the ritual performed. The second level is the line of march and supply. The army moved north along the axis of the Euphrates, taking the river craft and the crossings with it, and only shifted to wagons and pack animals where the water no longer carried; the king avoided committing his force to a general engagement in open, waterless country against the northern coalition. The coalition had more men but no single will: archers and loose troops gathered from the northern states along different axes, the garrisons of Yamahadi's towns held their own walls, and whenever the Babylonian main force turned on one city the others stood still, so that the alliance was never tactically an alliance at all. The third level is contact and siege. On contact, archers opened with curved fire over the front, spear infantry closed behind their shields in the centre and rear, and chariots struck the flanks and the gaps. Against towns he preferred blockade and the cutting of supplies first, bringing up towers and rams by slow degrees and only storming once a gate was broken; after the breach the usual practice followed, the walls pulled down, the divine images and the metal carried off, and the population dispersed. Destruction rather than occupation was the fixed conclusion of this style of expedition. The northern war was not flawless either: during an earlier siege of Malgium disease ran through his camp, and he had to lift the siege and withdraw, a reminder that this army of the north could fail.
data: 可核的數字大致如下。漢摩拉比在位四十三年，通行中年代把其統治定於約前1792至前1750年，修訂版則為前1784至前1742年，各家年代體系最遠可差近兩百年，因此本役的年序只能給出概數：戰爭落在其統治的最後數年，約當在位第三十三至三十四年，即馬里陷落之後。馬里書信保存了前1774至前1761年間的兩河政治往來，是同期記錄最密的段落；馬里窖藏出土的泥板逾兩萬片，其中漢摩拉比本人的信件就有數十封，北方遠征的經過與戰利品清單正靠這些泥板才得以重建。地理上，巴比倫至馬里直線約四百公里，順幼發拉底河行程超過五百公里；再往北至哈布爾河與巴利赫河谷，順河行程約九百至一千公里，超出車馱補給的極限。城邑規模方面，考古測量常引用馬里城牆高約四至五米、牆基厚可達二十餘米、周長約九至十公里的數字，可作同期城防的參照。兵員、陣亡與攻城耗時在同期文獻中完全沒有留下可靠記載，本節不列臆測數字；戰爭的月份亦無依據，編年只給年份，此處按兩河春末的行軍季節取四月。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked are roughly as follows. Hammurabi reigned for forty-three years; the middle chronology puts his rule at about 1792-1750 BCE and the revised chronology at about 1784-1742 BCE, and the several chronological schemes differ by nearly two centuries, so the order of events here can only be given approximately: the campaign falls in the last years of his reign, roughly his thirty-third and thirty-fourth regnal years, that is, after the fall of Mari. The Mari letters preserve the political traffic of the two rivers between about 1774 and 1761 BCE, the densest stretch of the period, and the excavations of Mari yielded more than twenty thousand tablets, among them several dozen letters in Hammurabi's own hand; it is on these tablets that the course of the northern expedition and its booty lists were reconstructed. Geographically, Babylon and Mari are about four hundred kilometres apart in a straight line and more than five hundred by the Euphrates; further north, to the Khabur and the Balikh valley, the journey along the river runs to something like nine hundred to a thousand kilometres, past the limit of what wagons and pack animals can carry. For the size of cities, excavation figures commonly quoted for Mari's enclosure wall put it at some four to five metres high, with a base thickness of over twenty metres and a circuit of roughly nine to ten kilometres, a useful reference for the fortifications of the age. Troop numbers, casualties and the length of the sieges leave no reliable trace whatever in the contemporary sources, and no speculative figures are offered here. The month of the campaign is equally unattested; the chronologies give only a year, and April is used here on the strength of the Mesopotamian campaigning season in late spring.
cause: 打起來是多層積累的結果。第一層是地緣：巴比倫在漢摩拉比手中先滅埃什努納、掃平拉爾薩、擊退埃蘭，馬里陷落後，幼發拉底河中游與北岸的商道盡入其手，北方最後一批城邦——舒拉魯姆、蘇巴爾圖與哈布爾河谷的諸邦——便直接暴露在巴比倫的推進方向上。第二層是方法：漢摩拉比已經定型了一套摧毀式遠征的作風，攻城之後拆毀城牆、搬走神像、遣散人口，而不是設官治理；毀掉一座北方城，等於拆掉對方重新集結的據點。第三層是象徵與資源：擄走達甘神像既是戰利品，也是把對方的祭祀秩序收入巴比倫的權力框架；北方山地的木材、銅料與通向地中海的商道，同樣在漢摩拉比的計算之內。第四層是雙方的體質：北方各邦沒有統一王權、常備軍與一致的指揮，靠共同的神祇與商路勉強維持盟約；巴比倫則有集中的王權、書吏官僚與神殿體系，能連續多年在多條戰線上遠征。第五層是時機：南方埃蘭戰爭仍在進行，漢摩拉比仍敢在北線用兵，正說明這套戰爭機器已經可以多線運作；他把北方當作收尾的一戰，而北方卻把它當作存亡之戰。
causeEn: The war came out of several layers of accumulation. The first is geography: with Eshnunna destroyed, Larsa swept away and Elam driven back, and with Mari fallen, the middle Euphrates and the trade routes of its north bank passed into Babylonian hands, and the last northern states - Surarrum, Shubartu and the towns of the Khabur valley - lay directly in the line of Babylonian advance. The second layer is method. Hammurabi had settled into a style of destructive expedition: after a siege the walls were pulled down, the divine images carried off and the population dispersed, rather than the city being taken over by officials; to destroy one northern city was to remove a base from which the enemy could gather again. The third is symbol and resources: carrying off the statue of Dagan was both booty and a way of drawing the rival's cult order inside the Babylonian frame, and the timber, the copper and the roads to the Mediterranean in the northern highlands were in Hammurabi's calculation as well. The fourth is the constitution of the two sides. The northern states had no unified kingship, no standing army and no consistent command, and held their alliance together only through shared gods and caravan roads; Babylon had a centralised kingship, a scribal bureaucracy and a temple establishment able to campaign for years on several fronts at once. The fifth is timing. The war with Elam was still running in the south, and Hammurabi could still send an army north, which shows that the machine could work on more than one front; he treated the north as a war to close, while the north treated it as a war for survival.
impact: 後果至少有四層。第一層在版圖：巴比倫的邊界被推到幼發拉底河上游的哈布爾與巴利赫河谷，這是兩河文明能有效控制的最西端；此後數百年，北方不再出現與巴比倫平行的城邦強國，直到中巴比倫時期亞述人從哈布爾河谷重新崛起，把這片曾被漢摩拉比掃平的區域變成日後支配兩河的基地。第二層在城邑：巴茲祖等要塞被拆毀，北方那套以城為節點、以神廟為中心的政治網絡被切斷，氏族與部落退回山地，北方的城市生活要等到亞述時代才重新出現。第三層在宗教與史料：達甘神像被擄往巴比倫並被安置在巴比倫的神廟體系中，此像其後如何處置、是否歸還，泥板有零星記載，說明搬動神像是當時的大事；而正是馬里書信的窖藏，保存了這場遠征的過程、戰利品清單與北方城名，是北部史僅存的系統性材料。第四層在制度：漢摩拉比把北方戰功寫進法典序言，以神授王權為統一提供解釋，刻於玄武岩石柱的《漢摩拉比法典》因此不只是法律文本，而是兩河第一次統一的政治宣言；其法理傳統後來被亞述、赫梯等國吸收改寫。
impactEn: The consequences run on at least four levels. The first is territorial: the Babylonian frontier was pushed to the Khabur and the Balikh valley at the head of the Euphrates, the westernmost limit the two-river civilisation could hold; for the centuries that followed no northern state rose to match Babylon, until in the Middle Babylonian period the Assyrians re-emerged from the Khabur valley and turned a region Hammurabi had swept into the base from which they would one day command the rivers. The second is the towns. Fortresses such as Bazazu were torn down, and the northern network of cities linked by cult centres was cut apart, the clans and tribes falling back into the hills, and urban life in the north did not return until the age of Assyria. The third is cult and record. The statue of Dagan was carried off to Babylon and installed in the Babylonian temple establishment, and the tablets give scattered notice of what became of the image afterwards and whether it was returned, which shows how the removal of a god was a matter of moment; and it is precisely the archive of Mari that preserves the course of the expedition, the booty lists and the names of the northern towns, the only systematic material for the history of the north. The fourth is institutional. Hammurabi wrote his northern victories into the prologue of his Code, supplying divine warrant for the unity, and the basalt stele carrying the laws became more than a legal text: it was the political proclamation of the first unification of the two rivers, and its legal tradition was later absorbed and rewritten by Assyria and Hatti.
result: 結局是巴比倫勝出。北方遠征達到目的：巴茲祖等城邑被攻破並拆毀，達甘神像連同金屬與器物被擄往巴比倫，亞馬海德一方的勢力退入山區，舒拉魯姆與蘇巴爾圖諸邦或降或散，幼發拉底河上游自此再無能與巴比倫相抗的政權。戰役之後數年，漢摩拉比回師南下，於約前1759年徹底擊敗埃蘭，兩河最後一個對手消失；前1750年他病逝於巴比倫，繼位者薩姆蘇伊盧納接手的是前1750年由他刻下的那根玄武岩石柱。需要說明的是：決戰的確切日期、雙方兵員、攻城日程與陣亡數目，在兩河同期文獻中一概沒有留下；能確定的，是這場遠征把巴比倫的邊界推到了胡里安山區的門戶之前，也把「摧毀北方城邑、擄走其神像」寫成了此後數百年近東列強的標準做法。
resultEn: The outcome was a Babylonian victory. The northern expedition achieved its purpose: towns such as Bazazu were stormed and torn down, the statue of Dagan was carried off to Babylon with the metal and the other valuables, the power of Yamahadi's side withdrew into the hills, and the states of Surarrum and Shubartu either submitted or scattered, so that the upper Euphrates no longer held any polity able to stand against Babylon. In the years after the campaign Hammurabi turned south, crushed Elam for good around 1759 BCE, and the last rival of the two rivers disappeared. He died at Babylon in 1750 BCE, and his successor Samsu-iluna inherited the basalt stele he had set up. It should be said plainly: the exact date of the decisive engagement, the troop strengths, the timetable of the siege and the casualty figures are simply not preserved in any contemporary source. What is certain is that this expedition pushed the Babylonian frontier up to the gateways of the Hurrian highlands, and wrote the destruction of the northern cities and the carrying off of their gods into the standard practice of the Near Eastern powers for the centuries that followed.
